title: The Measurements of Things Database — Overview: the measured world
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. A measurement is a number with a unit, an instrument, a method, and a source — without those four, it is trivia. This database gathers public measurements of all things: the constants that define the SI, the size and mass of Earth, the dimensions of bodies and everyday objects, the distances of astronomy, the properties of materials, and the ticks of time. Each record states the value, the unit, how it was measured, and where the number comes from, so any measurement here can be checked.
capabilities: Every measurement: value, unit, instrument, method, source
Constants, Earth, bodies, objects, stars, materials, time
Trivia vs measurement: the four companions

title: The Measurements of Things Database — Fundamental constants
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. The SI defining constants are exact by definition: the speed of light is 299,792,458 meters per second; the Planck constant is 6.62607015e-34 joule-seconds; the elementary charge is 1.602176634e-19 coulombs; the Boltzmann constant is 1.380649e-23 joules per kelvin; the Avogadro constant is 6.02214076e23 per mole. Measured constants with uncertainties include the gravitational constant G at about 6.67430e-11 m^3/kg/s^2. These numbers anchor every measurement on Earth — the meter is defined by light's travel, the kilogram by Planck's constant. Sources: BIPM SI Brochure, CODATA.
capabilities: Planck, charge, Boltzmann, Avogadro: exact SI definers
Gravitational constant G: measured, with uncertainty
Sources: BIPM SI Brochure, CODATA values

title: The Measurements of Things Database — Earth measurements
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Earth, measured: mass about 5.972e24 kilograms (from G and surface gravity); mean radius 6,371 kilometers; equatorial circumference about 40,075 kilometers; surface area about 510 million square kilometers. Highest: Mount Everest at 8,848.86 meters above sea level (2020 China-Nepal survey). Deepest: the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep near 10,935 meters. Mean surface temperature about 15 degrees Celsius; atmospheric pressure at sea level 101,325 pascals. Instruments: satellite gravimetry (GRACE), laser ranging, sonar bathymetry, barometers.
capabilities: Instruments: GRACE gravimetry, laser ranging, sonar

title: The Measurements of Things Database — Human body measurements
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. The human body, measured: core temperature about 37 degrees Celsius; resting heart rate typically 60 to 100 beats per minute; blood pressure near 120/80 mmHg; adult height averaging roughly 171 cm for men and 159 cm for women worldwide (varies strongly by country); total blood volume about 5 liters; about 206 bones in the adult skeleton; brain mass near 1.3 to 1.4 kilograms. These are population references, not prescriptions — individuals vary widely, and the database records ranges and sources rather than single ideals.
capabilities: Core temp ~37 C; resting pulse 60-100 bpm
Blood pressure ~120/80 mmHg; blood volume ~5 L

title: The Measurements of Things Database — Everyday object measurements
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Everyday things, measured: A4 paper is 210 by 297 millimeters, aspect ratio the square root of 2; a credit card is 85.60 by 53.98 millimeters (ISO/IEC 7810); a basketball's circumference is about 75 to 78 centimeters (NBA 29.5 inches); a soccer ball about 68 to 70 centimeters; a standard door in the US about 80 by 36 inches; a teaspoon holds about 5 milliliters; a sheet of printer paper weighs about 80 grams per square meter. Standards bodies — ISO, NBA, ASTM — are the sources behind the numbers.
capabilities: Sources: ISO, league rules, ASTM standards

title: The Measurements of Things Database — Astronomical measurements
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. The sky, measured: the astronomical unit is exactly 149,597,870,700 meters; a light-year is about 9.461 trillion kilometers; a parsec about 3.26 light-years. The Sun's mass is about 1.989e30 kilograms; its diameter about 1.39 million kilometers. Earth orbits at 1 AU with a year of 365.25 days; the Moon sits about 384,400 kilometers away, receding 3.8 centimeters per year (measured by lunar laser ranging). The observable universe spans about 93 billion light-years. Sources: IAU resolutions, NASA ephemerides.

title: The Measurements of Things Database — Material property measurements
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Materials, measured: water's density 1,000 kg/m^3 at 4 C; steel about 7,850; aluminum 2,700; gold 19,320; diamond hardness 10 on the Mohs scale, talc 1. Tensile strength: structural steel about 400 MPa, spider silk near 1,000 MPa by weight's champion. Thermal conductivity: copper about 400 W/m/K, air about 0.026. The speed of sound in air about 343 m/s at 20 C; in water about 1,480. Measured by densitometers, hardness testers, tensile machines, and guarded hot plates — instruments named per record.

title: The Measurements of Things Database — Time and frequency measurements
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Time, measured: the second is defined by 9,192,631,770 periods of cesium-133 radiation — counted by atomic clocks accurate to nanoseconds per day, with optical clocks pushing further. A mean solar day is 24 hours; a sidereal day about 23 hours 56 minutes; a tropical year about 365.2422 days. The quartz in a wristwatch vibrates at 32,768 Hz; mains electricity hums at 60 Hz in the Americas, 50 Hz elsewhere. Sources: BIPM, NIST time laboratories.
